session.summary: Exploration of a new journalism platform concept focused on creating a structured, computational back-end database for facts to enhance predictive power and insight in reporting.

records.title: A New Journalism Platform: Structured Fact Database
records.content: This record outlines a visionary idea for a new type of journalism platform that serves as a structured back-end database for facts, fundamentally transforming how journalism operates. The concept is not to compete with traditional journalism but to support it by mapping out detailed, structured data about global events, financial transactions, political appointments, conflicts of interest, and systemic issues like the revolving door and military-industrial complex. The platform aims to automate open-source investigation, leveraging technologies like LLMs to identify conflicts of interest, build probabilistic maps of events, and even predict outcomes through inference models. This structured data approach would enhance journalism's predictive power, generate insightful articles, and potentially integrate with social media for optimized content delivery.
records.description: Proposes a back-end database for journalism to structure facts for computational analysis and predictive insights.

sections.heading: Core Concept
sections.content: Journalism lacks a structured back-end database for facts, unlike other systems such as healthcare or law enforcement which store data computationally. This platform would serve as the back-end, mapping out intricate details of global happenings—financial transactions, political moves, conflicts of interest, and systemic issues like the military-industrial complex—making journalism more insightful and predictive.

sections.heading: Operational Mechanism
sections.content: The platform would function as an automated open-source investigator, integrating new information live and using large language models (LLMs) to detect potential conflicts and build probabilistic maps of events. By structuring data for computational availability, it could perform inference, predict outcomes, and even generate compelling articles tailored for audience engagement or social media optimization.

sections.heading: Comparison with Existing Systems
sections.content: Unlike Wikipedia, which focuses on notable entities, or traditional news archives which are unstructured transcripts of events, this platform would specifically structure ongoing global news data for analysis. It differentiates from existing amalgamated news sites by focusing on computational structuring rather than merely aggregating stories.
